transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my sleep has been really broken for a long time. I fall into bed exhausted, but I wake up at every little sound in the house, and then I’m up before the alarm anyway. I just don’t feel like I’ve rested.
How long have you been experiencing this pattern of waking up frequently and rising earlier than intended?
It’s been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us, a little over two years ago now.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly, gasp, or seem to stop breathing for moments while you're asleep?
No, no one’s mentioned anything like that to me.
Aside from feeling tired, do you find yourself worrying excessively about different things during the day—things like health, finances, or family—that's hard to control?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have things on my mind sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying about everything all day or that I can’t control it.
Over the past couple of months, have you noticed feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Most days, yes. It feels like the color has gone out of things. Even at Sunday dinner with my family, or when I’m looking at art I used to enjoy, I just don’t feel much from it. And sometimes I have to try not to tear up for no clear reason.
You mentioned feeling this low mood and loss of interest most days—how long has this been going on?
I’d say it started a little over two years ago, around when my mother-in-law moved in with us.
Over these past two years, has this low mood and loss of interest been present continuously, or have there been stretches of weeks or months where you felt back to your normal self?
It’s been pretty continuous since my mother-in-law moved in, a little over two years ago. I haven’t really felt like my old self for any long stretch.
During this two-year period, have you noticed significant changes in your appetite or weight, real trouble concentrating, or any thoughts about death or that life isn't worth living?
My appetite’s really dropped off. I mostly just pick at the food I make for everyone, or grab some toast after my shift. My clothes have been fitting looser, and I haven’t been trying to lose weight.
Over these two years, has the intensity of your low mood and other symptoms stayed fairly steady and mild, or have there been times when it became noticeably more severe than usual?
I’m not really sure how to judge that. It’s felt bad for a long time, but I can’t say there were clear periods where it suddenly got a lot worse than usual.
Over these past two years, have you noticed real trouble concentrating or making decisions, like at work or when reading?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a real problem with that. I mean, I can still follow what I’m doing at work and make the usual decisions.

Over these two years, has your low mood ever been severe enough to significantly interfere with your ability to work, care for your family, or maintain relationships, or has it stayed at a more mild-to-moderate level that you've been able to push through?

I’ve been able to keep going, but it takes a lot out of me. I’m falling behind on my client documentation, and I don’t volunteer to mentor the newer aides anymore like I used to. Just getting the basic work and things at home done feels like everything I have.
Over these past two years, have you ever had thoughts about death, that you'd be better off not being here, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean by thoughts about death. I know I’ve been feeling worn down, but I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Over these past two years, have you also noticed a persistent lack of energy or feeling fatigued nearly every day, beyond just the poor sleep?
Yes. By the time I’m done seeing my clients and get back home to help there, my body just feels heavy. Even things like finishing my notes or folding laundry can feel like too much to push through.
Over these past two years, have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have you felt physically restless or unable to sit still?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that myself.
Over these past two years, have you often felt worthless, or found yourself feeling excessively guilty about things, even minor things?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of myself as worthless, and I can’t say I’ve noticed feeling especially guilty about little things.
Over these two years, would you describe your low mood as a persistent, low-grade heaviness in the background, or has it felt like a more intense, full-blown depression that really weighs you down?

It’s more than just in the background. Most days, it feels like the color has gone out of things. Even at Sunday dinner with my family, or looking at art I used to enjoy, I can feel myself wanting to tear up for no clear reason.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient endorses a cluster of depressive symptoms—persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue, and sleep disturbance—present nearly every day for over two years, causing functional impairment (falling behind on documentation, withdrawal from mentoring role) but without psychotic features, suicidal ideation, or complete incapacitation, consistent with a moderate severity major depressive episode. Anxiety symptoms were explicitly denied (no excessive uncontrollable worry), making generalized anxiety disorder unlikely. While the chronicity (>2 years) raises consideration of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), the symptom count and intensity (5+ criterion symptoms, clear anhedonia, guilt-free but functionally impairing) meet full criteria for a major depressive episode of moderate severity rather than the more indolent, lower-grade dysthymic pattern.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood most days for over two years
Loss of interest/pleasure in previously enjoyed activities (family dinners, art)
Decreased appetite with unintentional weight loss (clothes fitting looser)
Persistent fatigue/low energy nearly every day
Sleep disturbance with frequent nighttime waking and early morning awakening

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms reported as continuous, nearly daily, for slightly over two years, beginning when mother-in-law moved into the household
additional_requirements: No manic or hypomanic episodes reported
No significant psychomotor agitation or retardation observed/reported
No feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt endorsed
No suicidal ideation or thoughts of death endorsed
Sleep apnea symptoms (snoring, gasping) denied, reducing likelihood of primary sleep disorder
Excessive uncontrollable worry denied, reducing likelihood of generalized anxiety disorder
